extracted.intended_audience: Researchers aspiring to professorship-level funding in Switzerland; prospective applicants to SNSF Professorial Fellowships; university research administrators
extracted.subtask_short: SNSF Professorial Fellowship eligibility and rules
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the merged PRIMA and Eccellenza schemes into the SNSF Professorial Fellowships, describing eligibility windows, funding ceilings, status requirements, gender-equality measures, and call timing for prospective applicants. Useful for researchers planning applications and institutional advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by highest-scoring applications
rubrics_metrics.description: As before for Eccellenza, the just over 30 researchers with the highest-scoring applications will be funded, regardless of gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition remains at least as challenging as before; selection is score-based and governed by the SNSF's stringent excellence criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed budget share for women / additional funding via PRIMA budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 14 projects by women will receive additional funding via the PRIMA budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that, in addition to the roughly 30 highest-scoring awards, up to 14 female-led projects receive funding from the reserved PRIMA budget, yielding around 45 fellowship holders in total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender equality measure integrated into scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The gender equality measure is now integrated directly into the SNSF Professorial Fellowships scheme; the existing PRIMA budget will continue to be reserved for women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective is to increase the share of women in key research positions (women currently account for 23% of professors); women no longer have to choose between two schemes, which should increase female application share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project funds ceiling (CHF 1 million) plus salary
rubrics_metrics.description: Project funds: maximum of CHF 1 million (PRIMA budget until now: CHF 750,000) plus grantee's salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eccellenza's higher ceiling (CHF 1M) is adopted to eliminate disparities between the former schemes; applicants should budget projects within this maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee status: assistant professor
rubrics_metrics.description: Status: assistant professor (status until now in PRIMA: at least group leader, or assistant professor depending on the higher education institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship holders will conduct their own research project with their own team at assistant professor level for five years; check institution-specific interpretations of 'assistant professor' where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call dates and submission period
rubrics_metrics.description: Call: 1 November – 1 February (for PRIMA until now: 1 August- 1 November).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should prepare for the new standardized annual call window; the first call's eligibility window will be extended by three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility time window after doctorate (standard and clinical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time window for submitting an application: up to 10 years after defending the doctoral thesis; for researchers doing clinical work: 14 years after the medical degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These windows replace the previous Eccellenza limits (8 years standard; 12 years clinical). For the first call the eligibility window will be extended by three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum research experience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum requirement: 3 years of research work after defending the doctoral thesis (PRIMA until now: 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate at least three years of post-PhD research experience in addition to satisfying the time-window rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection with Switzerland requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a connection with Switzerland (like Eccellenza).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement references the same 'connection with Switzerland' requirement used for Eccellenza; applicants should verify what constitutes an acceptable connection (host institution, employment/contract, etc.) in the formal call documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of PRIMA benefits such as flexible mobility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits PRIMA offered its exclusively female grantees, such as more flexible mobility criteria, were introduced in all schemes in 2020 when the SNSF implemented the DORA recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility previously afforded by PRIMA (e.g., mobility considerations) has been carried over into the unified scheme; applicants with non-linear career paths should consult the detailed call for how flexibility is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRIMA Leadership Programme access
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRIMA Leadership Programme is open to all female grantees of the SNSF Professorial Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Female fellowship holders will continue to have access to leadership development offered under PRIMA; applicants may consider this an added professional development benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of stringent excellence criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNSF's stringent excellence criteria will continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The merger does not relax scientific excellence requirements; applicants should expect high standards and strong competition when preparing proposals.
